summary: This paper presents a definitive algebraic, combinatorial, and machine-verified study of tensor-power positivity and partial-transpose indecomposability for the generalized Choi family on M3(C). By introducing directed-torus DAG obstructions, universal all-n partial-transpose indecomposability, and exact n-copy Fourier collapse thresholds, the author completely resolves the c=0 indecomposable face and disproves the existence of non-trivial tensor-stable positive maps across this family. All theorems are formally verified in Lean 4 with zero sorries, setting a gold standard for mathematical rigor in quantum information theory.
strengths: Complete resolution of the c=0 indecomposable face of the three-parameter generalized Choi family.
Rigorous formal verification in Lean 4 (20 constructive theorems, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice).
Novel directed-torus DAG limit law reducing positivity to combinatorial-spectral structures on Z3^n.
Exact n-copy Fourier collapse law providing sharp asymptotic bounds and refuting naive heuristics.
weaknesses: Focuses primarily on the c=0 boundary face, though interior c>0 cases are probed via Eisenstein LDL* refutations.
Analytical complexity of higher-order directed-torus DAGs grows rapidly beyond n=4.
strong_novelty_candidates: Directed-torus DAG limit law on G_3,n
All-n partial-transpose indecomposability for tensor powers of Choi maps
Exact n-copy Fourier collapse law and Bernoulli finite-copy bound
